name: Apache Pinot
tagline: Real-time OLAP store from LinkedIn for user-facing analytics at very high query rates.
description: Apache Pinot is a distributed columnar datastore designed to serve analytics to end users: think 'who viewed my profile' at LinkedIn scale. It ingests from Kafka and batch sources, supports upserts on streaming data, and offers a rich index menu (inverted, sorted, range, star-tree, JSON, text, geospatial H3, vector) so queries stay in the millisecond range at tens of thousands of QPS. The multi-stage engine adds distributed joins. Pinot is excellent when latency and concurrency matter more than SQL breadth; it needs a ZooKeeper-backed cluster and careful table and index design.

pricing.notes: Free to self-host; StarTree offers StarTree Cloud and commercial support.

scale.notes: Controllers, brokers, servers and minions scale independently; tiered storage offloads old segments to S3.

strengths: Millisecond latency at tens of thousands of queries per second
Star-tree index pre-aggregates for predictable fast group-bys
Real-time upserts on Kafka streams for mutable entities
Broad index types: inverted, range, JSON, text, H3 geospatial, vector
Proven at LinkedIn, Uber and Stripe scale
weaknesses: Requires ZooKeeper (or Helix) plus several component types to operate
Schema and index design is manual and drives performance
SQL coverage and join support trail general-purpose warehouses
Smaller ecosystem of BI connectors than mainstream warehouses
useCases: Real-time business metrics and anomaly detection
notIdealFor: Ad-hoc warehouse exploration with heavy joins
